summary: Split PlanetGenerator's `type` into its two jobs: it stays the FORMATION SEED (it legitimately decides radius, mass, atmosphere, moon count, palette) and a new derived `worldClass`, computed from the finished body's condition vector, becomes what every descriptive surface reads — the info panel, the orrery, and the seed search. Same bug shape as the volatile-delivery split just shipped.

baseline.measuredOn: 2026-09-04, 200 seeds `rocky-0..199`, 476 solid planets (gas excluded via compositionClass)
baseline.misnamedEarthLikes: 11 of 14 carry a name other than ocean/terrestrial
baseline.oceanLabelled: 7 bodies, 0 warm-and-wet, median surface T 355 K
baseline.lavaLabelledButCold: 15 of 45 below 400 K (3.2 % of all solid)
baseline.gates: warm = surface T in [250, 320] K; wet = composition.volatileFraction >= 0.12 (e1Regime BAND.V_MIN, the engine's own constant); rocky = compositionClass(cv) !== 'gas'
baseline.whyNotInSeededBand: the engine's inSeededBand() adds an Earth-MASS gate 0.6-1.6 M⊕ which cuts the 14 to 5. Max ruled 2026-09-04 that warm wet super-Earths count, so the classifier carries its own size bound. All 14 sit below 1.4 R⊕, so a radius-valley cut at 1.8 R⊕ is non-binding on today's population — it is there to stop a future 2.5 R⊕ water world being called habitable, not to filter the current one.
baseline.whyNotHabitabilityD15: PhysicsEngine.habitabilityScore has NO volatile/water term. Measured: 189 of the 462 non-habitable bodies score at or above the lowest genuinely warm-and-wet one; venus-labelled bodies median 0.80. Unusable as a classifier.
baseline.anchorSeed: rocky-126 planet 2 ('PVX J3DK6GAO+RBJGI5M c') — the exact world Max UAT'd on 2026-09-04 with 'yep, it works'. Water 0.310, surface 293 K, and the game calls it an Ice World.

design.seam: PlanetGenerator.js:822 already builds `const condition = conditionFromBody(planetData)` from the finished record. `worldClass` is derived THERE — no new seam is cut and no second adapter is written.
design.vocabulary: REUSES the existing names (gas-giant, hot-jupiter, sub-neptune, carbon, lava, venus, ice, ocean, terrestrial, rocky) so no UI copy, colour table or filter option changes shape.
design.guardrail: `worldClass` must never become an input to physics — that would rebuild the loop this workstream exists to cut. It is written last, after every physical quantity is final, and carries a comment saying so at both the write site and PlanetGenerator's `type` declaration.
design.reuse: every gate reads an already-exported engine function or named constant (compositionClass, icenessOf, biosphereOf, BAND.V_MIN, the BIO_T_* band) rather than a fresh hand-written bound.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: No world carries a name its own physics flatly contradicts — every world called an ocean world actually has water on it, no lava world is cold, no ice world is boiling.

verifyVia.input: Re-run the 200-seed census (census.mjs) over the generator, headless.
verifyVia.observable: Zero bodies classed `ocean` or `terrestrial` fail the warm-and-wet gates (baseline 7); zero classed `lava` sit below 400 K (baseline 15); zero classed `ice` sit above 273 K (baseline 6). census.mjs exits non-zero while any remain.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The 14 genuinely warm, wet worlds are the ones the galaxy calls habitable — today 11 of them are called something else.

verifyVia.observable: All 14 warm-and-wet bodies carry a `worldClass` of `ocean` or `terrestrial` (baseline 3), and no body outside that set does (baseline 7 false positives).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Nothing about how the planets look, how big they are, or how many moons they have changed.

verifyVia.input: Regenerate the same 200 seeds and diff every generated field except the new one; run the draw-stream instrument (Instrument B).
verifyVia.observable: Byte-identical radius, mass, moon count, rings, palette and atmosphere on all 476 bodies, and ZERO seeds move their per-yield draw profile. `worldClass` is the only added key. (Trap #15: a fresh `new SeededRandom(...)` moves the draw stream with no values moved — use `namespacedFloat` if any draw is needed at all; the intent is that none is.)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When I fly to a warm wet world, the panel tells me that is what it is, instead of calling it a rock.

verifyVia.input: In the running game, load ?system=rocky-126 and select the second planet — the exact world Max UAT'd on 2026-09-04 — then repeat on rocky-61 (carbon) and rocky-151 (rocky).
verifyVia.observable: The info panel's type line reads Ocean World or Terrestrial, not Rocky World / Ice World / Carbon World.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: I can spot a habitable world on the system map before I fly to it.

verifyVia.input: Open the orrery on that same seed.
verifyVia.observable: The habitable world's dot is drawn in the ocean/terrestrial colour (blue/green), distinguishable from the rocky and ice dots around it. Both planetColors sites in NavComputer read the derived class.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When I ask the game to find me a habitable planet, the ones it hands me are habitable.

verifyVia.input: Run the seed search with the 'Habitable Planet' filter.
verifyVia.observable: Every system it returns contains at least one body that passes the warm-and-wet gates; today the filter reads the formation roll and returns systems whose only 'ocean' is hot and dry.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Flying around, the galaxy tells me what its worlds are, and I can find a place worth going to.

verifyVia.input: Max flies the live build, looks at several worlds and goes looking for a habitable one.
verifyVia.observable: Holistic: the names the galaxy gives its worlds cohere with what he finds when he gets there, and finding somewhere worth visiting feels possible rather than random.

inputs: PlanetGenerator.generate() — the finished planetData record, after every physical quantity is computed
conditionFromBody(planetData) at PlanetGenerator.js:822 — the existing, already-built condition vector; the ONE named seam game data enters the engine through
e1Regime.compositionClass(cv) — already derives gas / carbon / icy / rocky from physics
e1Regime BAND.V_MIN (0.12) — the engine's own wet threshold
surfaceMaterial.biosphereOf(cond) + icenessOf(cond) — the life-cover and frozen-over laws the shader already reads
conditionFromBody.surfaceTemperatureOf — the greenhouse correction, so the classifier reads SURFACE temperature, not the game's bare equilibrium number
outputs: ui/BodyInfo.js:58 — PLANET_TYPE_NAMES lookup (the info panel type line)
ui/NavComputer.js:2331 and :2978 — both planetColors tables (the orrery dots)
main.js:8462 — the 'habitable' case of the seed-search filter, currently `type === 'terrestrial' || type === 'ocean'`
ui/DebugPanel.js:482 — the 'Habitable Planet' filter option this drives
mustStayWorking: The formation roll itself — _pickType stays exactly as it is, including its Kepler occurrence rates. It still chooses radius range, estimateMassEarth, atmosphere strength, cloud/ring chance, max moon count and the legacy palette.

The shared RNG draw stream — no new draw on it. Instrument B counts draws on SeededRandom.prototype.rng across EVERY instance, so even a side-draw sub-rng moves the per-yield profile (trap #15). The derived class needs no randomness at all.

conditionFromBody's rule that the adapter reads `type` for NOTHING — the derived class is computed on the game side FROM the condition vector; the label must not start crossing that seam in the other direction.
The world-engine render path — no planet's appearance changes. The lab planet material carries no planetType uniform; this is confirmed, not assumed.
MoonGenerator._pickType and moon labels — out of scope this pass; moons keep their formation labels until planets prove the shape.

The exotic-overlay types (fungal, city-lights, ecumenopolis, hex, machine, crystal, shattered) are applied AFTER natural generation and are not physical classes. They must survive the split without being re-derived away.

All 858 line-anchored citations into PlanetGenerator — editing this file drifts every one of them (trap #16). Repair by locating the SYMBOL, never by bumping the integer; some refs use the short `:539 `symbol`` form a naive File.js:NNN search misses.
